canvas.title: Explainable ENSO predictability from climate mode interactions

nodes.body_md:
# Introduction

## What makes long-lead ENSO skill hard to explain?

# XRO model

## How does XRO make ENSO–mode interactions explicit?

## Skill without process attribution

### ENSO skill past one year stays hard, and AI skill is still hard to tie to named physics
- ENSO supplies most seasonal forecast skill, yet sources of skilful long-lead predictions remain elusive.
- Remote modes (NPMM/SPMM, IOB/IOD/SIOD, TNA/ATL3/SASD) can help, but prior CGCM and LIM tests struggle to quantify relative basin shares.
- AI forecasts can reach ~18–24 months without a clear physical process link.

## L blocks and nRO baseline

### XRO couples an ENSO recharge oscillator to eight remote SST modes through $\mathbf{L}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{L}_{\mathrm{ENSO}}&\mathbf{C}_1\\\mathbf{C}_2&\mathbf{L}_M\end{pmatrix}$
- $\mathbf{X}_{\mathrm{ENSO}}=[T_{\mathrm{ENSO}},h]$ uses Niño3.4 and equatorial WWV; $\mathbf{X}_M$ holds NPMM, SPMM, IOB, IOD, SIOD, TNA, ATL3, SASD.
- $\mathbf{L}_{\mathrm{ENSO}}$ is internal recharge–discharge; $\mathbf{C}_1$ feeds remote modes into ENSO; $\mathbf{C}_2$ sends ENSO teleconnections outward; $\mathbf{L}_M$ is remote-mode memory/damping.
- Seasonally modulated $\mathbf{L}$ and $\mathbf{N}$ plus red-noise forcing yield a 515-parameter fit; nRO keeps only tropical-Pacific dynamics as the no-coupling baseline.

# Efficacy boosted by climate interactions

## Does XRO deliver explainable skill at 16–18 months?

# Sources outside the tropical Pacific

## Which remote basins actually add ENSO forecast skill?

# ENSO intensification from remote sources

## How do remote modes intensify El Niño and La Niña?

# Predictability reduced by model biases

## Which CGCM biases most hurt ENSO forecasts?

# Discussion

## What must climate models get right for better ENSO forecasts?

## Three remote-mode requirements

### XRO’s gain over nRO resides in remote initial-condition memory under an unbiased operator
- Models need correct ENSO recharge–discharge dynamics plus remote-mode initial conditions, seasonally modulated memory/damping, and seasonally modulated teleconnections to ENSO.
- Process-level SSTA-budget bias tracing with XRO can guide model development.
- Higher-frequency MJO–WWB coupling and decadal predictability pathways are stated outlook, not demonstrated here.

## Fit length and noise limits

### The framework is low-order and observation-length constrained
- A robust seasonal fit uses ~40–50 years for 515 free parameters.
- Multiplicative state-dependent noise is acknowledged but hard to estimate from the available record.
- Satellite-era/ORAS5 control skill is the main showcase; XRO2 pantropical/type forecasts are supportive extensions.

## Same amplitude, different precursors

### The 1997–1998 and 2015–2016 El Niños share Niño3.4 size but not WWV, IOD, or NPMM preconditioning
- Similar peak Niño3.4 can arise from different Pacific recharge and remote SSTA patterns.
- Those precursors reshape later basin evolutions and global precipitation impacts.
- That contrast motivates attributing forecast skill to specific climate-mode pathways.

![Source figure](xro-fdbd2de637c3d4.webp)

## Long-lead skill vs nRO, IRI/NMME, and AI

### XRO reproduces ENSO statistics and keeps Niño3.4 correlation above 0.5 at an 18-month lead
- A 43,000-year stochastic run matches observed seasonality, skewness, spectrum, WWV lead, and remote-mode lead–lag links.
- Out-of-sample reforecasts beat IRI dynamical multi-model means beyond ~9 months and match top AI skill.
- Control 1979–2022 skill stays AI-comparable at long leads, and the spring predictability barrier is much weaker than in nRO.

![Source figure](xro-505e6b33fbb0f9.webp)

## Uninitialized memory attribution

### Extra skill comes mainly from remote-mode initial-condition memory, not ENSO-triggered coupled feedbacks alone
- Only uninitialized basin tests give nearly additive ExPO/IO/AO skill shares; decoupling overestimates each basin.
- Mode interactions raise correlation skill by up to ~0.2 and weaken the spring barrier.
- ExPO (NPMM), IO (IOD), and AO (TNA/SASD) contribute with distinct seasonal windows.

![Source figure](xro-3d08cf932eb109.webp)

## NPMM, IOD, and TNA pathways

### NPMM, IOD, and TNA are the main remote amplitude sources beyond Pacific recharge–discharge
- Control XRO extends skilful event occurrence and amplitude prediction to ~6–18 months versus uninitialized/decoupled ExPO+IO+AO runs.
- Spring NPMM charges WWV; opposite IOD events shift Niño3.4 by about 0.4–0.5 °C ~15 months later; TNA typically cools Niño3.4 by ~0.3 °C at 6–12 months.
- Peak-phase composites credit NPMM, IOD, and TNA as the leading extras, with large inter-event spread.

![Source figure](xro-1e59e518db5b54.webp)

## Correct $\mathbf{L}_{\mathrm{ENSO}}$ and $\mathbf{C}_1$ first

### CMIP-trained XROm skill lags observations; fixing ENSO dynamics and inbound feedbacks helps most
- XROm trained on 91 CMIP historical runs is consistently less skilful and more spread out than observation-trained XRO.
- Swapping in observed $\mathbf{L}_{\mathrm{ENSO}}$ raises Niño3.4 skill at all leads; correcting inbound $\mathbf{C}_1$ helps intermediate leads up to ~16 months.
- Correcting outbound $\mathbf{C}_2$ helps remote modes such as the IOD more than Niño3.4 itself.

![Source figure](xro-796eb427e70f92.webp)
